newsitem.title: USA: TWA said mulling winter schedule cutbacks.
newsitem.headline: TWA said mulling winter schedule cutbacks.

text.p: Trans World Airlines Inc is considering winter schedule cutbacks, primarily in New York, in both domestic and international markets, the pilots' union said Wednesday.
The union expects the first quarter flying schedule, which will outline these seasonal cuts, to be released by the end of the week.
Service that it scaled back during the winter, however, may be restored as the airline increases operations in the spring, the union said.
TWA management is reviewing all aspects of the company, including fleet composition, route profitability and general operations, the union said.
The airline is also considering trimming international service in some "thin markets," the pilots' union said. The union declined to comment on which markets would be slated for cutbacks.
TWA did not immediately return calls seeking comment.
The union also said it expects TWA to announce a new chief executive before a December 10 board meeting.
TWA's chief executive Jeffrey Erickson will leave the carrier in January after about 2-1/2 years in the post.
